[276.2, 75.8, 356.7, 100.3] font=TimesNewRomanPS-BoldItal size=22.1 color=0x0 : Abstract
[84.0, 128.6, 542.2, 140.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : AirPulse is a Big Data Analytics project designed to analyze and simulate cascading flight delays across
[84.0, 147.8, 542.3, 160.1] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : the national airspace network. It models airports as nodes and scheduled flights as directed edges using
[84.0, 166.8, 539.7, 179.0] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : a Dynamic Directed Multigraph. An adapted Kermack-McKendrick SIR (Susceptible-Infectious-
[84.0, 185.8, 542.6, 198.0] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : Recovered) epidemic model is used to simulate delay propagation and recovery across interconnected
[84.0, 204.7, 168.8, 216.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : airports. Using R,
[170.7, 205.6, 209.3, 216.7] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=10.1 color=0x0 : data.table
[209.3, 204.7, 235.3, 216.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : , and
[237.2, 205.6, 262.8, 216.7] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=10.1 color=0x0 : igraph
[262.7, 204.7, 542.4, 216.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : , the system efficiently processes large-scale flight data and
[84.0, 223.7, 542.5, 235.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : performs network analysis. It calculates Degree Centrality, Betweenness Centrality, and PageRank to
[84.0, 242.6, 542.5, 254.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : develop a Composite Super-Spreader Index, which identifies critical airports that may contribute to
[84.0, 261.6, 542.4, 273.8] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : widespread delay propagation. AirPulse also simulates ground-stop scenarios to understand delay
[84.0, 280.6, 542.5, 292.8] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : transmission, airport vulnerabilities, and recovery patterns. The project provides a network-based
[84.0, 299.5, 542.5, 311.7] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : approach to analyzing aviation delays and supports improved understanding of airspace resilience and
[84.0, 318.5, 169.5, 330.7] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : delay management.
[84.0, 379.1, 140.0, 392.4] font=TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : Keywords:
[143.0, 379.9, 545.4, 392.1] font=TimesNewRomanPS-ItalicMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : Big Data Analytics, Air Traffic Delay, Dynamic Directed Multigraph, Epidemic Modeling,
[84.0, 399.6, 545.4, 411.8] font=TimesNewRomanPS-ItalicMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : SIR Model, Network Centrality, PageRank, Betweenness Centrality, Delay Propagation, Aviation
[84.0, 418.6, 172.0, 430.8] font=TimesNewRomanPS-ItalicMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : Network Resilience.

[60.0, 115.0, 79.6, 132.8] font=TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT size=16.1 color=0x0 : 1.1
[96.0, 115.0, 183.5, 132.8] font=TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT size=16.1 color=0x0 : Background
[72.0, 151.8, 577.6, 165.1] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : The aviation industry operates through a highly interconnected network of airports and scheduled flights,
[72.0, 172.4, 577.6, 185.7] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : where delays at one airport can affect operations at several others. Late-arriving aircraft, crew
[72.0, 193.1, 577.6, 206.4] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : dependencies, and limited turnaround time can cause delays to propagate across multiple flight routes.
[72.0, 213.7, 577.6, 227.0] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : Traditional flight delay analysis focuses on individual flights and often overlooks these interconnected
[72.0, 234.6, 577.6, 247.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : relationships. AirPulse addresses this challenge by modeling the national airspace as a Dynamic Directed
[72.0, 255.2, 577.6, 268.5] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : Multigraph and applying an adapted SIR epidemic model to analyze how delays spread and recover across
[72.0, 275.9, 176.6, 289.2] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : the aviation network.
[60.0, 342.6, 79.6, 360.4] font=TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT size=16.1 color=0x0 : 1.2
[96.0, 342.6, 174.6, 360.4] font=TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT size=16.1 color=0x0 : Motivation
[71.4, 374.7, 577.6, 388.0] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : The motivation behind AirPulse is to understand how flight delays spread across interconnected airports
[71.4, 395.4, 577.6, 408.7] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : rather than treating each delay as an independent event. In real-world aviation, a delay at one major airport
[71.4, 416.0, 577.6, 429.3] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : can affect aircraft, flight crews, and subsequent flights, resulting in a chain of secondary delays. AirPulse
[71.4, 436.9, 577.6, 450.2] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : addresses this problem by modeling airports as nodes and scheduled flights as directed connections in a
[71.4, 457.5, 577.6, 470.8] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : network. By using Big Data Analytics, graph-based analysis, and an adapted SIR epidemic model, the
[71.4, 478.2, 577.6, 491.5] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : project aims to identify critical airports, analyze delay propagation, and understand how delay cascades
[71.4, 498.8, 351.7, 512.1] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : develop and recover across the national airspace network.

[43.1, 228.3, 577.6, 241.6] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : then used to construct a Dynamic Directed Multigraph, in which airports are represented as nodes and scheduled
[43.1, 249.0, 443.2, 262.3] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : flight routes are represented as directed edges. Network analysis is performed using
[442.8, 250.7, 468.4, 261.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=10.1 color=0x0 : igraph
[468.3, 249.0, 577.6, 262.3] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : to calculate important
[43.1, 269.9, 577.6, 283.2] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : measures such as Degree, Betweenness Centrality, PageRank, and the Composite Super-Spreader Index (Ψ).
[43.1, 290.5, 577.6, 303.8] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : These measures help identify airports that can have a significant role in the propagation of delays. An adapted
[43.1, 311.1, 577.6, 324.4] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : SIR epidemic model is then applied to represent airports as susceptible, infected, or recovered based on delay
[43.1, 331.8, 577.6, 345.1] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : conditions. The model simulates how a delay originating at one airport can spread to connected airports and
[43.1, 352.7, 577.6, 366.0] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : how the affected airports gradually recover. Finally, the analytical and simulation results are processed through
[43.1, 373.3, 418.7, 386.6] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : the FastAPI backend and presented through an interactive Next.js dashboard
[418.7, 373.3, 421.7, 386.6] font=TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : ,
[421.7, 373.3, 577.6, 386.6] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : allowing users to visualize the
[43.1, 393.9, 326.3, 407.2] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : airport network, rankings, and delay-propagation behavior.

[85.0, 737.3, 381.0, 749.5] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=11.0 color=0x0 : Pillai HOC College of Engineering and Technology (Autonomous),

[36.0, 150.3, 577.6, 163.6] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : AirPulse provides a Big Data Analytics-based approach for understanding and analyzing the propagation of flight
[36.0, 171.0, 577.6, 184.3] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : delays across an interconnected national airspace network. The system represents airports as nodes and scheduled
[36.0, 191.6, 577.6, 204.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : flight routes as directed edges, creating a Dynamic Directed Multigraph that captures the relationships between
[36.0, 212.5, 577.6, 225.8] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : different airports. Large-scale flight data from the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) is processed
[36.0, 233.1, 95.2, 246.4] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : using R and
[94.7, 234.9, 133.3, 246.0] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=10.1 color=0x0 : data.table
[133.3, 233.1, 168.4, 246.4] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : , while
[167.9, 234.9, 193.4, 246.0] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=10.1 color=0x0 : igraph
[193.4, 233.1, 577.6, 246.4] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : is used for network analysis. Measures such as Degree, Betweenness Centrality,
[36.0, 253.8, 577.6, 267.1] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : PageRank, and the Composite Super-Spreader Index (Ψ) help identify important airports that can influence delay
[36.0, 274.4, 577.6, 287.7] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : propagation. The adapted SIR epidemic model further simulates the spread of delays by representing airports as
[36.0, 295.3, 577.6, 308.6] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : susceptible, infected, and recovered states. The project demonstrates how an initial delay or ground stop can
[36.0, 315.9, 577.6, 329.2] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : propagate through connected airports, increase overall delay impact, and eventually reduce as recovery
[36.0, 336.6, 577.6, 349.9] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : mechanisms take effect. Overall, AirPulse shows how combining Big Data processing, graph analytics, and
[36.0, 357.2, 577.6, 370.5] font=TimesNewRomanPSMT size=12.0 color=0x0 : epidemic modeling can provide a better understanding of cascading flight delays and critical network bottlenecks.
